readings.title: Bread from Heaven
readings.subtitle: The Provision of Manna and Quail
readings.text: [Exodus 16:1] And they departed from Ělim, and all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl came to the Wilderness of Sin, which is between Ělim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their going out of the land of Mitsrayim. [2] And all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl grumbled against Mosheh and against Aharon in the wilderness. [3] And the children of Yisra’ĕl said to them, “If only we had died by the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the land of Mitsrayim, when we sat by the pots of meat and when we ate bread to satisfaction! For you have brought <dn>את</dn> us out into this wilderness to starve all this assembly to death.” [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am raining bread from the heavens for you. And the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, in order to try them, whether they walk in <dn>My</dn> Torah or not.</dq> [5] <dq>“And it shall be on the sixth day that they shall prepare <dn>את</dn> what they bring in, and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily.”</dq> [6] And Mosheh and Aharon said to all the children of Yisra’ĕl, “At evening you shall know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim. [7] “And in the morning you shall see <dn>את</dn> the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> hears <dn>את</dn> your grumblings against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And what are we, that you grumble against us?” [8] And Mosheh said, “In that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gives you meat to eat in the evening, and in the morning bread to satisfaction, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> hears <dn>את</dn> your grumblings which you make against <dn>Him</dn>. And what are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [9] And Mosheh said to Aharon, “Say to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Come near before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> has heard your grumblings.’ ” [10] And it came to be, as Aharon spoke to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, that they looked toward the wilderness and see, the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared in the cloud. [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> the grumblings of the children of Yisra’ĕl. Speak to them, saying, ‘Between the evenings you are to eat meat, and in the morning you are to be satisfied with bread. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq> [13] And it came to be at evening that quails came up and covered <dn>את</dn> the camp. And in the morning the dew lay all around the camp. [14] And when the layer of dew lifted, there on the surface of the wilderness was a small round substance, as fine as frost on the ground. [15] And the children of Yisra’ĕl saw, and they said to each other, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. And Mosheh said to them, “It is the bread which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given you to eat. [16] “This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded: <dq>‘Let every man gather it according to each one’s eating, an omer for each being, according to the number of your beings. Let every man take for those who are in his tent.’</dq> ” [17] And the children of Yisra’ĕl did so and gathered, some more, some less. [18] And they measured it by the omer, and he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack. Each one gathered according to his eating. [19] And Mosheh said, “Let no one leave any of it until morning.” [20] And they did not listen to Mosheh, for some of them left part of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. And Mosheh was wroth with them. [21] And they gathered it every morning, each one according to his eating. And when the sun became hot, it melted. [22] And it came to be, on the sixth day, that they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each one. And all the rulers of the congregation came and told Mosheh. [23] And he said to them, “This is what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said, <dq>‘Tomorrow is a rest, a set-apart Shabbat to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Bake <dn>את</dn> what you bake, and boil <dn>את</dn> what you boil. And lay up for yourselves <dn>את</dn> all that remains over, to be kept until morning.’</dq> ” [24] And they laid it up till morning, as Mosheh commanded. And it did not stink, and no worm was in it. [25] And Mosheh said, “Eat it today, for today is a Shabbat to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, today you do not find it in the field. [26] “Six days you gather it, but on the seventh day, which is the Shabbat, there is none.” [27] And it came to be that some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather, but they found none. [28] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“How long shall you refuse to guard <dn>My</dn> commands and <dn>My</dn> Torot?</dq> [29] <dq>“See, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given you <dn>את</dn> the Shabbat, therefore <dn>He</dn> is giving you bread for two days on the sixth day. Let every man stay in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.”</dq> [30] So the people rested on the seventh day. [31] And the house of Yisra’ĕl called <dn>את</dn> its name Manna. And it was like white coriander seed, and the taste of it was like wafers with honey. [32] And Mosheh said, “This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded: <dq>‘Fill an omer with it, to be kept for your generations, so that they see <dn>את</dn> the bread with which <dn>I</dn> fed <dn>את</dn> you in the wilderness, when <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> you out of the land of Mitsrayim.’</dq> ” [33] And Mosheh said to Aharon, “Take a pot and put an omer of manna in it, and lay it up before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to be kept for your generations.” [34] As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh, so Aharon laid it up before the Witness, to be kept. [35] And the children of Yisra’ĕl ate <dn>את</dn> the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate <dn>את</dn> the manna until they came to the border of the land of Kena‘an. [36] And an omer is one-tenth of an ephah.

readings.title: Water from the Rock
readings.subtitle: Massa and Meriḇah
readings.text: [Exodus 17:1] And all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl departed from the Wilderness of Sin, journeying on their stages according to the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and camped in Rephiḏim. And there was no water for the people to drink. [2] And the people strove with Mosheh, and said, “Give us water to drink.” And Mosheh said to them, “Why do you strive with me? Why do you try <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [3] And the people thirsted there for water, and the people grumbled against Mosheh, and said, “Why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim, to kill <dn>את</dn> us and <dn>את</dn> our children and <dn>את</dn> our livestock with thirst?” [4] And Mosheh cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “What am I to do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me!” [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Pass on before the people, and take with you some of the elders of Yisra’ĕl. And take in your hand your rod with which you struck <dn>את</dn> the river, and go.</dq> [6] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am standing before you there on the rock in Ḥorĕḇ. And you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it, and the people shall drink.”</dq> And Mosheh did so in the eyes of the elders of Yisra’ĕl. [7] And he called the name of the place Massah and Meriḇah, because of the strife of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and because they tried <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in our midst or not?”

readings.title: Victory over Amaleq
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Nissi
readings.text: [Exodus 17:8] And Amaleq came and fought with Yisra’ĕl in Rephiḏim. [9] And Mosheh said to Yehoshua, “Choose for us men and go out, fight with Amaleq. Tomorrow I am standing on the top of the hill with the rod of <dn>Elohim</dn> in my hand.” [10] And Yehoshua did as Mosheh said to him, to fight with Amaleq. And Mosheh, Aharon, and Ḥur went up to the top of the hill. [11] And it came to be, when Mosheh held up his hand, that Yisra’ĕl prevailed. And when he let down his hand, Amaleq prevailed. [12] But Mosheh’s hands were heavy, so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. And Aharon and Ḥur supported his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side. And his hands were steady until the going down of the sun. [13] And Yehoshua defeated <dn>את</dn> Amaleq and <dn>את</dn> his people with the edge of the sword. [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Write this for a remembrance in the book and recite it in the ears of Yehoshua, that <dn>I</dn> shall completely blot out <dn>את</dn> the remembrance of Amaleq from under the heavens.”</dq> [15] And Mosheh built an altar and called its name, <dn>YeHoVaH Nissi</dn>; [16] for he said, “Because a hand is on the throne of <dn>Yah</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is to fight against Amaleq from generation to generation.”

readings.title: Yithro’s Visit
readings.subtitle: Sacrifice and Rejoicing
readings.text: [Exodus 18:1] And Yithro, the priest of Miḏyan, Mosheh’s father-in-law, heard of all that <dn>Elohim</dn> had done for Mosheh and for Yisra’ĕl <dn>His</dn> people, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had brought <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl out of Mitsrayim. [2] Then Yithro, Mosheh’s father-in-law, took <dn>את</dn> Tsipporah, the wife of Mosheh, after he had sent her back, [3] and <dn>את</dn> her two sons, of whom the name of one was Gĕrshom, for he said, “I have been a sojourner in a foreign land,” [4] and <dn>את</dn> the name of the other was Eli‘ezer, for he said, “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.” [5] And Yithro, Mosheh’s father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife to Mosheh in the wilderness, where he was encamped at the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [6] And he said to Mosheh, “I, your father-in-law Yithro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons with her.” [7] And Mosheh went out to meet his father-in-law, and bowed down and kissed him. And they asked each other about their welfare, and they went into the tent. [8] And Mosheh told his father-in-law <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had done to Pharaoh and to the Mitsrites for Yisra’ĕl’s sake, <dn>את</dn> all the hardship that had come upon them on the way, and how <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had delivered them. [9] And Yithro rejoiced for all the good which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had done for Yisra’ĕl, whom <dn>He</dn> had delivered from the hand of the Mitsrites. [10] And Yithro said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who has delivered <dn>את</dn> you from the hand of the Mitsrites and from the hand of Pharaoh, and who has delivered <dn>את</dn> the people from under the hand of the Mitsrites. [11] “Now I know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is greater than all the elohim, for in the matter in which they acted proudly, <dn>He</dn> was above them.” [12] And Yithro, Mosheh’s father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and slaughterings for <dn>Elohim</dn>. And Aharon and all the elders of Yisra’ĕl came to eat bread with Mosheh’s father-in-law before <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: Counsel for Governance
readings.subtitle: Appointing Judges over Yisra’ĕl
readings.text: [Exodus 18:13] And it came to be on the next day, that Mosheh sat to judge the people. And the people stood before Mosheh from morning until evening. [14] And Mosheh’s father-in-law saw <dn>את</dn> all that he did for the people, and said, “What is this thing that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit by yourself, and all the people stand before you from morning until evening?” [15] And Mosheh said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to seek <dn>Elohim</dn>. [16] “When they have a matter, they come to me, and I judge between one and another, and I make known <dn>את</dn> the laws of <dn>Elohim</dn> and <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> Torot.” [17] And Mosheh’s father-in-law said to him, “The thing that you are doing is not good. [18] “Both you and this people with you shall certainly wear yourselves out. For this matter is too heavy for you. You are not able to do it by yourself. [19] “Now listen to my voice, let me counsel you, and <dn>Elohim</dn> be with you: Stand before <dn>Elohim</dn> for the people, and you shall bring the matters to <dn>Elohim</dn>. [20] “And you shall enlighten <dn>את</dn> them concerning the laws and the Torot, and show them <dn>את</dn> the way in which they should walk and <dn>את</dn> the work which they do. [21] “But you yourself, seek out from all the people able men, such as fear <dn>Elohim</dn>, men of truth, hating unfair gain. And place these over them to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens. [22] “And they shall judge <dn>את</dn> the people at all times. And it shall be that they bring every great matter to you, but they themselves judge every small matter. So make it lighter for yourself, for they shall bear with you. [23] “If you do this thing, and <dn>Elohim</dn> has commanded you, then you shall be able to stand, and all this people also go to their place in peace.” [24] And Mosheh listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said. [25] And Mosheh chose able men out of all Yisra’ĕl, and made them heads over the people: rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens. [26] And they judged <dn>את</dn> the people at all times – <dn>את</dn> the hard matters they brought to Mosheh, but they judged every small matter themselves. [27] And Mosheh sent his father-in-law away, and he went his way to his own land.

readings.title: Israel at Sinai
readings.subtitle: Preparation for the Covenant
readings.text: [Exodus 19:1] In the third month after the children of Yisra’ĕl had gone out of the land of Mitsrayim, on this day, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai. [2] For they departed from Rephiḏim, and had come to the Wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. And Yisra’ĕl camped there before the mountain. [3] And Mosheh went up to <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> called to him from the mountain, saying, <dq>“This is what you shall say to the house of Ya’aqoḇ, and inform the children of Yisra’ĕl:</dq> [4] <dq>‘You have seen <dn>את</dn> what <dn>I</dn> did to the Mitsrites, and how <dn>I</dn> bore <dn>את</dn> you on eagles’ wings and brought <dn>את</dn> you to <dn>Myself</dn>.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And now, if you diligently obey <dn>My</dn> voice and shall guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant, then you shall be <dn>My</dn> treasured possession above all the peoples – for all the earth is <dn>Mine</dn> –</dq> [6] <dq>‘and you shall be to <dn>Me</dn> a kingdom of priests and a set-apart nation.’ These are the words which you are to speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl.”</dq> [7] And Mosheh came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them <dn>את</dn> all these words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded him. [8] And all the people answered together and said, “All that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken we shall do.” So Mosheh brought back <dn>את</dn> the words of the people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn. [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am coming to you in the thick cloud, so that the people hear when <dn>I</dn> speak with you, and believe you forever.”</dq> And Mosheh reported <dn>את</dn> the words of the people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Go to the people and set them apart today and tomorrow. And they shall wash their clothes,</dq> [11] <dq>and shall be prepared by the third day. For on the third day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall come down upon Mount Sinai in the eyes of all the people.</dq> [12] <dq>“And you shall set bounds for <dn>את</dn> the people all around, saying, ‘Take heed to yourselves that you do not go up to the mountain or touch its border. Whoever touches the mountain shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [13] <dq>‘Not a hand touches it, but he shall certainly be stoned or shot with an arrow, whether beast or man, he shall not live.’ When the trumpet sounds long, let them come near the mountain.”</dq> [14] And Mosheh came down from the mountain to the people and set <dn>את</dn> the people apart, and they washed their clothes. [15] And he said to the people, “Be prepared by the third day. Do not come near a woman.” [16] And it came to be on the third day, in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain. And the voice of a shophar was very strong, and all the people who were in the camp trembled. [17] And Mosheh brought <dn>את</dn> the people out of the camp to meet with <dn>Elohim</dn>, and they stood at the foot of the mountain. [18] And Mount Sinai was in smoke, all of it, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> descended upon it in fire. And its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace, and all the mountain trembled exceedingly. [19] And when the voice of the shophar sounded long and became very strong, Mosheh spoke, and <dn>Elohim</dn> answered him by voice. [20] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came down upon Mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> called Mosheh to the top of the mountain, and Mosheh went up. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to see, and many of them fall.</dq> [22] <dq>“And let the priests also who come near <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set themselves apart, lest <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> break out against them.”</dq> [23] And Mosheh said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “The people are not able to come up to Mount Sinai, for <dn>You</dn> warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around <dn>את</dn> the mountain and set it apart.’ ” [24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Come, go down and then come up, you and Aharon with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, lest <dn>He</dn> break out against them.”</dq> [25] And Mosheh went down to the people and spoke to them.
